source: ASH 2020 SCD Guidelines + WHO SCD management resource (representative protocol)

indication_criteria: ≥3 VOC per year requiring medical attention
All children ≥9 months (ASH 2020 universal HU recommendation for HbSS)

penicillin.indication: All HbSS/HbS-beta-thal from 2 months of age
penicillin.note: Continue indefinitely if spleen has auto-infarcted or splenectomy performed

malaria_prophylaxis.indication: All SCD patients in endemic regions

tcd_classification.abnormal_action: Refer urgently for chronic transfusion programme or HU intensification — stroke risk >10% per year
tcd_classification.conditional_action: Repeat TCD in 3 months; ensure HU optimised

voc_mild.management: Oral NSAIDs (ibuprofen/diclofenac), oral paracetamol, high oral fluids ≥2L/day, warm compress, rest
voc_mild.escalate_if: No relief in 2h, pain worsening, fever, vomiting

voc_moderate.management: IV access, IV fluids 1.5× maintenance, oral or IV morphine 0.05–0.1 mg/kg, anti-emetic, O2 if SpO2 <94%
voc_moderate.escalate_if: Pain uncontrolled at 1h, signs of ACS (cough, pleuritic chest pain, fever + new CXR infiltrate)

voc_severe.management: Hospital admission, IV morphine PCA or regular dosing, IV fluids, blood group & crossmatch, incentive spirometry, haematology consult

crisis_management.acs_management: Admit urgently, O2 to maintain SpO2 ≥95%, IV fluids (not aggressive), empiric antibiotics (cover Mycoplasma/Chlamydia), exchange transfusion if deteriorating, incentive spirometry
crisis_management.splenic_sequestration_action: Urgent transfusion to raise Hb by 2 g/dL (not fully correct — risk of hyper-viscosity). Splenectomy referral for recurrent episodes.
crisis_management.stroke_action: Immediate exchange transfusion targeting HbS <30%. CT/MRI brain. Chronic transfusion programme post-stroke.

vaccination_requirements: Pneumococcal conjugate + polysaccharide (PCV13 then PPSV23 at ≥2 years)
